editions.title: Federal Probe Spooks Chelsea Billionaire Owners

stories.headline: Chelsea Co-Owners In Talks To Sell Their Shares To Majority Owner Clearlake Capital
body: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are exploring the sale of their 12.8% stakes to private equity firm Clearlake Capital, the club's 61.5% majority owner.
The potential move follows strained relations between the partners, who originally bought the English soccer club for £2.3B in 2022.
This follows Walter recently selling his Los Angeles Lakers ownership for $12.5B while facing a federal investigation into his insurance businesses.

stories.headline: Sports Tech Startup Peripheral Raises $8.7M To Expand Its Viewing Platform
body: Investment firms Inovia Capital and Deloitte Ventures co-led the $8.7M funding round to support the growing technology startup.
Peripheral builds spatial intelligence software, a specialized technology that creates highly immersive and interactive experiences for live sporting events.

stories.headline: NBA Ad Revenue Hits Record $2.1B In First Year Of New TV Deal
body: Advertisers spent $2.11B on NBA games in 2025-26, up 38% from $1.53B the prior season.
The league moved games from cable to broadcast TV on NBC and ABC, lifting average viewership 16% to 1.78M.
Amazon's Prime Video, a new partner, sold $507.4M in ads and drew viewers a decade younger than traditional TV.

stories.headline: Sheffield United Faces Potential Ownership Loss Over Unpaid $47M Debt
body: Former ownership group United World claims the current American buyers still owe $47M from their $135M purchase of the football club.
United World filed a court petition after the buyers allegedly transferred shares to a new holding company to avoid paying the remaining balance.
If the court grants this petition, the current owners will lose control of the team and face a severe 12-point league penalty.

stories.headline: New Wave Of Unregulated NIL Agents Upends College Football With Multimillion-Dollar Contracts
body: A&P Sports Agency, a Texas startup representing student-athletes, negotiated over $30M in deals as direct school payments replaced basic marketing endorsements.
These new reps charge up to 20% in commissions, angering traditional NFL agents who are strictly capped at 3% by union rules.
Lawmakers recently proposed the Protect College Sports Act to cap agency fees at 5% and stop predatory practices in this unregulated market.

stories.headline: GSE Worldwide Launches New Sports Advisory Division And Hires Industry Veteran
body: The sports marketing firm created this new group to help brands and investors decide where to spend their money in sports.
Michael Brown, an executive with 30 years of marketing experience at major global brands, will lead the new division.
The team will initially help North American companies maximize their sports sponsorships before expanding to international markets.

stories.headline: Enhanced Group Posts $62M Quarterly Loss Following Expensive Debut Event
body: The controversial sports and health company lost $62M last quarter, largely due to the massive costs of hosting its inaugural Las Vegas competition.
To reduce expenses moving forward, the business will host smaller sporting events and expand its growing telehealth services and health supplement divisions.
Despite going public in May at a $1.2B valuation, shares of the startup backed by billionaire investor Peter Thiel have crashed 84% this year.

stories.headline: Sports Brand Owner Amer Sports Reports $1.63B In Revenue And Raises Future Outlook
body: Sports brand owner Amer Sports saw its second-quarter revenue jump 32% to $1.63B and profits rise to $127M.
This financial boost was driven by strong global sales from its popular outdoor and athletic brands like Arc'teryx, Salomon, and Wilson.
Because of this continued momentum, the company raised its 2026 forecast and now expects 24% in total revenue growth.

stories.headline: University of Tennessee Basketball Signs $3M Annual Jersey Sponsorship With Axle Logistics
body: Local shipping company Axle Logistics, founded by university alumni, will sponsor both basketball teams' jerseys through the 2030-31 season.
The agreement pays the athletic department over $3M annually, providing crucial new revenue to help the school remain competitive.
This partnership also funds marketing campaigns to help student-athletes build their personal brands and gain real business experience.

stories.headline: ESPN Co-Founder Bill Rasmussen Dies At 93
body: Rasmussen launched ESPN in 1979 after being fired by hockey's New England Whalers, betting that fans wanted sports coverage around the clock.
To fund the launch, he sold 85% of ESPN to oil giant Getty Oil, whose new owners pushed him out in 1980.
Despite his early departure, Rasmussen reconciled with the network in 1999 and entered the Sports Broadcasting Hall of Fame.

stories.headline: US Women’s Sports Viewership Surges As Advertising Spend Jumps 120 Percent
body: Nielsen, a major media tracking firm, reports fans watched 28.6B minutes of women's sports in early 2026, an 18% yearly increase.
This growing audience pushed sponsor values up 71% for the WNBA basketball league, while overall ad spending jumped 120% since 2022.
The boom attracted 16M new sports fans who are deeply loyal, with 60% willing to switch brands based on corporate values.

stories.headline: Formula One Owner Liberty Media Defends Commercial Expansion To Secure Younger Audiences
body: F1's owner, US-based Liberty Media, is pushing to modernize the sport through new racing rules, additional American events, and lucrative global brand deals.
Traditional fans criticize this rapid commercialization, but executives argue expanding beyond an aging European base is strictly necessary for long-term survival.
To reach these new viewers, F1 is experimenting with unconventional broadcasts on tech giant Apple and a massive $600M Hollywood movie.

stories.headline: NFL Commissioner Confirms League Will Eventually Add International Teams
body: Roger Goodell, head of the National Football League, stated he has zero doubt that franchises will one day operate outside the United States.
The American football league is expanding globally, scheduling a record nine overseas games in 2026 across new cities like Paris and Melbourne.
Goodell noted that an overseas city must first successfully host a permanent team before the league considers playing a Super Bowl championship there.

stories.headline: Dick’s Sporting Goods Expands Into The Individual Sports Trading Card Market
body: The US retailer is buying individual sports cards at trade shows to build interactive hobby shops inside its massive sporting goods stores.
Executives noticed card collectors visit stores more frequently, chasing a lucrative market that earned retail competitor Target $1B in revenue last year.
To generate buzz for this new venture, the company recently purchased a rare autographed baseball rookie card at auction for $1.11M.

stories.headline: Tennis Star Aryna Sabalenka Hits $50M In Career Earnings Following Early Financial Struggles
body: Early in her career, massive travel costs forced Sabalenka and her team to share cheap hotel rooms despite her earning nearly $2M annually.
Performance coach Jason Stacy and head coach Anton Dubrov helped by taking low base salaries tied to a percentage of her tournament winnings.
As the top-ranked player, she now makes over $8.2M a year in prizes plus lucrative sponsorships with major global brands like Gucci.
